name: morph-nav
summary: A segmented tab bar whose active pill is one shared element re-parented into the tab you click, springing across at bounce 0.2 over 350ms while the panel below crossfades and tweens its height to the new content.

bounce.description: Overshoot on the pill's spring. Upstream's spring({ bounce }).

duration.description: Milliseconds the pill takes to reach the new tab. Upstream's spring({ duration }).

fade.description: Milliseconds of the panel crossfade. Upstream's enterFrom/leaveTo duration.

enterDelay.description: Milliseconds the incoming panel waits before fading up. Upstream's enterFrom delay.

deviations.what: Both createLayout calls take this mount's own elements instead of the selectors 'nav ul' and '.content', and the click handler is an element listener instead of document.onclick.
deviations.why: A selector finds the first match in the whole document, so two of these sections on one page would both drive the first one's bar, and document.onclick is a single slot that the second mount would overwrite. The listener also re-checks that the tab closest() found belongs to this section, because closest() walks out past the section boundary.

deviations.what: Under prefers-reduced-motion the click handler still runs and still swaps the pill and the panel; only the two createLayout instances are skipped.
deviations.why: Effect contract: mount() stays at rest -- but a tab bar's switching is its function, not its decoration. Returning early the way a particle field does would leave a control that looks interactive and does nothing. Skipping the layouts removes the spring and the crossfade and leaves the swap instant, which is what the preference asks for.

deviations.what: The eight planet buttons and their data-color keys become four data-panel keys, and the buttons carry role=tab / aria-selected / aria-controls inside a role=tablist with role=tabpanel on the panels.
deviations.why: The planets are the example's content, not its effect. The roles are what make the control announce itself: upstream's markup is a plain button list, so a screen reader gets no signal about which entry is current or what it controls, and this library ships sections into real sites.

deviations.what: Upstream's demo chrome and its var(--bg-2) / var(--color-1) palette are replaced with a dark section, an eyebrow, a heading and --fx-* custom properties.
deviations.why: The palette variables come from the examples' shared assets/css/styles.css, which is not part of this port, and the effect ships as a section rather than a centred demo page. Every structural rule -- the nav bar, the relative list, the absolutely-inset pill, the z-index swap on the active button, display:none / display:block on the panels -- is upstream's and carries the effect.

deviations.what: Inactive tab labels are #b8c1d4 rather than upstream's var(--fg-2), and panel body copy is #c2cadb.
deviations.why: Upstream's foreground token is defined in a stylesheet this port does not carry, so the values had to be chosen here; both clear the 4.5:1 floor this library holds text to against the bar and card behind them.
